### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-record-context`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-record-context/README.md`, `packages/services/service-record-context/src/plugin.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx`  _(via aiContexts (symbol, a field of const object STACK_DEFINITION_COLLECTIONS_SHAPE))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-record-context/README.md`, `packages/services/service-record-context/src/plugin.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1f023e762f1b84f7bfa3368284989bd045a21ec7` — the merge of head `e9b2056f9dab8ebf46b5f1de19ab1a0ffe729a0c` into base `ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1f023e762f1b84f7bfa3368284989bd045a21ec7 && git checkout 1f023e762f1b84f7bfa3368284989bd045a21ec7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f e9b2056f9dab8ebf46b5f1de19ab1a0ffe729a0c && git checkout -B drift-repro ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f && git merge --no-ff e9b2056f9dab8ebf46b5f1de19ab1a0ffe729a0c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ff6f9768d2969c4f2f42819f461424965238e30f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- **Dev flag, size (1454 against an estimate of 600 to 800): answered.** The card's What 2 names the route (detail into a reference where a ceiling binds) and amendment 2 claims the row. ### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-ai/references/context-packs.md`**, every teaching sentence against `main`:

Step 4c on `main` also refuses the whole call when the target of a listed lookup fails the read guard (a system object that does not attest AI reads). It refuses every caller, so it shows on the first test call. One clause would cover it, paid for in the same file.
- N2 (nit) — "master-detail" in the `related.object` row is the prose spelling; the field type is `master_detail`. The spec's own describe uses the same prose, so nothing is wrong, only less greppable.

**`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`**: the five-line section, the tool row and the frontmatter are true and point at the reference. **`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`**: the `record-context` cell and "context packs" in the ADR-0150 list are true (the ADR-0150 addendum of 2026-11-25 on `main`). The three cuts are restatement: the `crm_` prefix rule in the `manifest.namespace` paragraph, `task.object.ts` in the naming table and the barrel example, and "handed to the stack key of its name" in The Template bullet. The sentence the `check:skill-top-level-keys` self-test pins is present at the head. A cross-skill relative link has precedent in this file.

**`skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json`**: case 11 is well-formed (ids 1 to 11, the same four keys as its siblings). `gradeAnswer` is two case-sensitive `String.includes` filters. An answer that follows `expected_output` (the reference's example plus `requires: ['record-context']`) holds all seven `must_contain` tokens and none of the three forbidden ones, so it passes. The `expected_output` prose itself is not graded.
- N3 (nit) — `must_not_contain: "aiReadable"` is a bare word. A correct answer that says in prose that no `aiReadable` is needed would fail. The sibling cases forbid code spellings with a colon or a paren.

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`**: the new describe is true against `capability-providers.ts` and `plugin.ts`, and corrects the old sentence that read the token as the only serving condition (scope note N1). The README and the docblock now teach both doors (N2), and the README example is still a valid stack.

No must-fix. The teaching matches the code on `main`. S1 concerns the card's close, not the diff.
